# Kern navigation — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for Kern navigation when the app needs its destinations: drawer, rail, bar and sidebar pane unified on one destination contract. `sections` are destination data — key, label, icon, badge, disabled — shared by all four variants, with a route-manifest adapter building them from a route manifest, and `variant` picks the surface: the transient drawer-modal sheet, the icon-edge rail, the compact-screen bar, or the persistent sidebar pane for desk layouts. `header` and `footer` slot the workspace switcher and the user row, `detail` carries the drill pane on sidebar-pane, and `floating` docks a floating action button above the bar — above, never inside. There is no destination tree — one flat set per surface — no resize or collapse gesture, since `railMode` is the host's responsive decision, and no routing inside: `value` and `onValueChange` report the key and the host navigates. Destinations keep their surface's contract, with the bar and rail announcing tabs with selected state and the drawer a labelled dialog list, and exactly one destination is current while the modal drawer selects-then-dismisses, so choosing always lands.

## Native

### Features

Reach for Kern navigation when the app needs its destinations: drawer, rail, bar and sidebar pane unified on one destination contract — the native twin under the same contract. `sections` are destination data — key, label, icon, badge, disabled — shared by all four variants, with `variant` defaulting to the bar on native while the drawer, rail and sidebar-pane render the same contract in their own surfaces. `header` and `footer` slot the switcher and user row on rail and sidebar-pane, `floating` docks a floating action button above the bar, and `detail` stays unset on native — detail goes in a sheet, since a phone has no drill pane. There is no destination tree, no resize gesture, and no routing inside: `value` and `onValueChange` report the key and the host navigates. Native falls back to the first enabled destination, so something is always current and never nothing, and the modal drawer selects-then-dismisses, so choosing always lands.
